# A symbolic unique-base obstruction to the fixed-half-mass moment centroid

This is an exact obstruction to the proposed selector, not a counterexample
to OC. It uses n=1 and d=2. The fixed moment mass is precisely M/2^n=M/2.
Only one integer base has any feasible moment body at that mass, yet the
ordinary centroid of that moment body has depth strictly below the OC
constant. Thus arbitrary-base, maximum-marginal-depth, maximum-moment-body-
volume, and existential-base variants of this particular selector all fail.

No numerical computation is used in the proof. A separately verified
rational polygon enclosure is retained as an independent certificate in
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/three-simplex-moment-rational-certificate.json`, checked by
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify-three-simplex-moment-rational-certificate-density-adversary.py`.

## 1. The actual convex body and exact masses

Let

    K=conv{v0,v1,v2},
    v0=(-1/3,-1/3), v1=(2/3,-1/3), v2=(-1/3,2/3).

It has area 1/2 and centroid zero. Put

    a=1/8,       c=257/256,
    k=1-(a+c)/2=223/512,
    s=k v0=(-223/1536,-223/1536).

At integer bases -1,0,1 prescribe the fibers

    K_-=s+aK,       K_0=K,       K_+=s+cK,

and let C be their convex hull in R x R^2. These are exactly its three
integer fibers. Indeed

    (K_-+K_+)/2 = k v0+(1-k)K subset K,

so averaging the endpoint fibers does not enlarge the prescribed middle
fiber. Every point in the convex hull over base zero is a convex combination
of a point of K and such an endpoint midpoint, and therefore lies in K.
The extreme fibers cannot change. The base projection is [-1,1], so there
are no other integer fibers. C is compact, convex, and has nonempty ambient
interior, because the middle triangle and any point of an endpoint fiber
span R^3.

Let mu be the sum of ordinary areas on these fibers. The three masses are

    w_-=1/128,       w_0=1/2,       w_+=66049/131072.

Consequently

    M=132609/131072,       t=M/2=132609/262144.        (1)

For an integer j, define the fixed-mass balanced moment body

    B_t(j)={ t^(-1) integral x d sigma :
             0<=sigma<=mu, sigma(S)=t,
             integral z d sigma=t j }.

It is a compact convex set when nonempty: write sigma=f mu, use weak-star
compactness of 0<=f<=1, and impose the closed mass and moment constraints.
Every point of B_t(j) belongs to the actual fiber C_j, by convexity of C.

Both endpoint masses are strictly less than t. Since a measure supported
on bases [-1,1] can have base mean -1 or 1 only if it lies entirely on that
endpoint, B_t(-1)=B_t(1)=empty. Bases outside [-1,1] are impossible as well.
The middle base is the unique weighted median, since

    w_-<t,   w_+<t,   w_-+w_0>t,   w_0+w_+>t.

We will compute the centroid of the nonempty two-dimensional body B_t(0).

## 2. Two elementary facts about selected moments of a triangle

For a convex body L and a mass 0<v<=|L|, write

    Z_v(L)={v^(-1) integral x f(x)dx:
               0<=f<=1, integral f=v}.

These sets are compact and convex. They have nonempty interior when
0<v<|L|: for theta=(v/|L|)^(1/2), the sets
(1-theta)p+theta L, p in L, are contained in L and have mass v. Their
centroids range over the full-dimensional translate
(1-theta)L+theta g_L.

Fix a nonzero linear functional u and define the maximum unnormalized
selected moment

    R_L(v)=max{integral (u dot x) f(x)dx:
                         0<=f<=1, integral f=v}.

If a top cap with threshold q has mass v*, then the exchange inequality
proves, for every allowable mass v,

    R_L(v) <= R_L(v*)+q(v-v*).                       (2)

In fact (u dot x-q)(f-1_cap)<=0 pointwise; integrate and maximize over f.
At v*=|L|, the same formula holds with q=min_L u, taking the whole body
as the cap. Threshold level sets have area zero, so closed and open top
caps have the same mass here. Existence and uniqueness of the threshold
at an interior prescribed mass follow from continuity and strict increase
of the projection distribution inside its interval of support.

We also need only two coarse quantile bounds. Normalize u on K to range
from 0 to 1. A top cap of relative mass p has threshold at least

    1-sqrt(p).                                       (3)

A bottom cap of relative mass delta has threshold at most

    sqrt(delta).                                    (4)

For (3), choose a maximizing vertex v. The homothetic triangle
(1-sqrt(p))v+sqrt(p)K has relative area p and lies in the cap where the
normalized functional is at least 1-sqrt(p). Hence that cap has area at
least p, and the threshold selecting exactly p cannot be smaller.
The analogous homothetic triangle about a minimizing vertex proves (4).
These proofs apply to every functional, including those constant on an
edge of K.

## 3. Every support direction saturates the small endpoint fiber

Base balance at j=0 forces equal endpoint selected masses ell. The middle
selected mass is t-2ell. Feasibility means

    max(0,(t-w_0)/2) <= ell <= w_-=1/128.             (5)

The upper endpoint in (5) is feasible; all three resulting masses are
positive and respect their fiber capacities. Set m=w_- and

    m0=t-2m,
    p=m/w_+=a^2/c^2,
    delta=1-m0/w_0=(1-c^2+3a^2)/2=2559/131072.       (6)

For a fixed nonzero u, the support optimization at mass ell is

    F_u(ell)=R_(K_-)(ell)+R_K(t-2ell)+R_(K_+)(ell).

At ell=m, let q_- be min_(K_-) u, let q_+ be the top-cap threshold in K_+
selecting mass m, and let q_0 be the top-cap threshold in K selecting mass
m0. Apply (2) in the three fibers. It gives, for every feasible ell,

    F_u(ell) <= F_u(m)+(q_-+q_+-2q_0)(ell-m).        (7)

We prove that D=q_-+q_+-2q_0 is strictly positive. Let b=min_K u and let
L=max_K u-min_K u>0. The quantile bounds (3)--(4) imply

    q_-=u dot s+a b,
    q_+>=u dot s+c b+c L(1-sqrt(p)),
    q_0<=b+L sqrt(delta).

Since c sqrt(p)=a, their combination yields

    D >= (2-a-c)(u dot v0-b)
             +L[c-a-2sqrt(delta)].                  (8)

The first term is nonnegative because v0 belongs to K and 2-a-c>0.
The second term is strictly positive. Indeed c-a=225/256>0 and

    (c-a)^2-4delta=45507/65536>0.                     (9)

Thus D>0 for every nonzero u. Equations (5) and (7) show that each support
functional of B_t(0) is maximized using ell=m: the small endpoint fiber
is completely selected, regardless of the continuous direction.

This proves equality of compact convex bodies

    B_t(0) = (2m/t)s
                +(mc/t) Z_(m/c^2)(K)
                +(m0/t) Z_(m0)(K).                 (10)

To verify the coefficients directly, the full small fiber has continuous
first moment m s. A mass-m selection in s+cK has first moment
m s+mc z with z in Z_(m/c^2)(K). The middle selection contributes
m0 z0 with z0 in Z_(m0)(K). Dividing the sum by t proves that the right
side is exactly the feasible fixed-ell body. All support maxima occur
there by (7), which proves (10). The middle selected mass lies strictly
between 0 and |K|, so (10) has nonempty interior and its ordinary area
centroid is defined.

## 4. Its ordinary centroid is exactly computable by symmetry

Every linear map permuting the three vertices of the centered triangle K
preserves K and its ordinary area measure. Therefore it preserves each
selected-moment body Z_v(K). The same is true of their positively scaled
Minkowski sum on the right side of (10). The centroid of that sum is fixed
by every such linear map, because ordinary centroids commute with invertible
linear transformations. The only vector fixed by every vertex permutation
of a centered nondegenerate triangle is zero. For example, averaging the
three cyclic permutations sends every vector to zero, since the vertices
span the plane and have sum zero. Thus the unshifted sum has centroid zero.

Consequently the unique point prescribed by the fixed-mass selector is

    y=(2m/t)s=(-1784/397827,-1784/397827).             (11)

Both coordinates are strictly less than -1/250, since 1784*250=446000 is
larger than 397827. The point (0,y) is an actual point of S: it lies in
B_t(0) subset K. The obstruction concerns depth, not membership.

## 5. A closed oblique cap violates the selector's claimed guarantee

Take the fixed closed halfspace

    H={ (z,x1,x2): x1+x2+z <= -1/125 }.              (12)

It contains (0,y) by (11). On the left fiber,
max(x1+x2+z)=-959/768<-1/125, so the whole fiber is retained. On the right
fiber, min(x1+x2+z)=31/768>-1/125, so nothing is retained.
On the middle standard triangle, translate coordinates by (1/3,1/3).
The cap is the nonnegative-coordinate triangle with coordinate sum at
most 2/3-1/125=247/375. Therefore

    mu(H)=1/128+(1/2)(247/375)^2
         =4045201/18000000.                         (13)

For n=1,d=2, the OC constant is (1/2)(2/3)^2=2/9. Its target here is

    (2/9)M=44203/196608.

The exact positive deficit is

    (2/9)M-mu(H)=872713/9216000000>0.                (14)

All fibers are full dimensional, q=d=2, and the halfspace is a closed
halfspace of the full three-dimensional ambient space. No boundary mass
or limiting convention affects (13).

## 6. Exact scope of the obstruction

This proves that the ordinary centroid of the fixed-mass moment body
B_(M/2^n)(j) need not meet the OC constant. Here every integer base except
j=0 has an empty such body, so choosing a different feasible or deep base
cannot repair this selector. The existing sharp continuous or intrinsic
parity-density selection theorems do not force this moment-body centroid
to have the desired depth.

The example does not show that every point of B_t(0) fails, and does not
show that S has no OC center. It disproves only the specific deterministic
rule taking the ordinary volume centroid of B_(M/2^n)(j), even with free
choice of the integer base j. Any continuation of that route needs a new
point-selection mechanism or a different invariant.
